sections.title: Build the main window and transitions

inlineContent.text: Show progress while the sky and clouds load, and offer a retry if loading fails. Connect the view state to the loading operation, then build the feedback people see.
The main window lets people enter and leave the immersive view. Loading feedback and the space toggle will appear below the screen title.
Connect the main window to the opening and dismissal actions provided by SwiftUI. The
received through
lets the window and immersive view share state.
State injection and space registration are completed in the final chapter. Until then, use the preview in the next step to check the layout.

transfers the cache’s result into view state. It marks the start of a request as loading, success as ready, and failure with an error message. Initial loading and retry use the same function for consistent handling.
The function isn’t called automatically yet. Connect it to the view’s appearance at the end of this section.
displays feedback for the current loading state.
shows that assets are being prepared, so the app doesn’t appear unresponsive. The loading indicator disappears when preparation completes. Add failure feedback in the next step.
allows each state to display a different kind of view.

If asset preparation fails, show both a short explanation and the underlying error. The short message identifies the situation, and the details can help locate a missing file or incorrect setting. Use the message stored in
for this feedback.
The retry button, labeled ‘다시 시도’ in the sample app, lets people request asset preparation again. Its
connects the button to the asynchronous
function. A successful retry updates the same view state and removes the error feedback.
requests asset preparation when the main window appears. Preparing the sky and clouds before the person presses the button reduces waiting after entering the immersive view.
The task can run again when the view reappears. The
function from the previous chapter prevents duplicate loading: it returns if the assets are ready or waits for an existing task.

tasks.title: Create the space toggle and error messages

inlineContent.text: Use the button to communicate the action currently available. Prepare its title, enabled state, and error message separately before connecting them to the UI. Implement the actual space transition in the next section.
stores feedback for a failure to open the immersive view. Keeping this separate from asset loading errors identifies which operation failed. A value of
means there is no transition error to display.

chooses a label for the current space state. When closed, the app offers ‘구름 위로 올라가기’ (go up to the clouds); when open, it offers ‘땅으로 내려오기’ (return to the ground). During a transition, the label describes the operation in progress.

determines whether the button is available. A transition can begin only when the assets are ready and the space is fully open or closed. Disable the button during loading or a transition to reduce duplicate requests.

handles requests from the space toggle. The UI calls this function, and the function will choose whether to open or close the space based on its current state. This step provides the connection point; the next section implements the behavior.
The space toggle uses
to describe the next action and
to reflect availability. The
in the button action lets it request an asynchronous transition.
The connected function is still empty, so pressing the button doesn’t open the space yet.
Feedback below the button explains a space transition failure.
displays the
only when an error message is stored, leaving no error message visible otherwise. The next section stores this message when handling transition results.
